scope: Replay-manifest provenance and integrity controls; excludes correctness of the underlying mathematical theorem except where evidence provenance is misrepresented.
assets: Replay inputs and their exact content

trust_boundaries.trust_assumption: The writer is not assumed to be a trusted execution attestation; it can only record observed paths and hashes.
Commit SHA identifies a repository object, but does not prove that the stated command ran against that commit.
A reviewer can independently recompute hashes if referenced files are available, but a self-contained manifest is not self-authenticating.
No immutability or retention guarantee exists unless separately implemented and audited.

adversary_capabilities: Modify an input or output file after manifest creation
Edit manifest fields and recompute its ordinary digest
Provide a syntactically valid but semantically misleading status or scope
Replace both file and manifest when the same storage/control boundary is compromised
Supply an arbitrary commit identifier without proving the replay used it
Omit files, checks, limitations, or dependencies if generation is not independently constrained
out_of_scope_capabilities: Compromise of cryptographic primitives such as SHA-256
Compromise of a separately controlled signing key (no signing key is currently defined)
Proof of maliciousness or correctness of the mathematical model itself
controls_currently_present: SHA-256 recorded for listed inputs and artifacts
Manifest generator rejects missing files and malformed commit/status/dependency entries
Separate validator checks schema-like structure and semantic consistency
Optional file hash recomputation detects changed referenced files
known_gaps: Manifest is unsigned and can be replaced
Timestamp is generated locally and is not externally trusted
Git commit field is caller-supplied, not tied to runtime checkout
Input/artifact lists are manually supplied and not proven complete
No CI execution attestation or environment lockfile digest is required
Paths are not canonicalized to protect against aliases or symlink ambiguity
Hash checks do not establish numerical correctness
No immutable storage or chain-of-custody procedure

threats.name: Post-recording input mutation
threats.impact: Replay may be represented as using input content that has since changed.
threats.residual: Detection depends on retaining accessible original files and trusted expected hashes.

threats.name: Artifact mutation or substitution
threats.impact: Reported output may not match the originally recorded artifact.
threats.current_detection: Optional hash recomputation against artifact paths.
threats.residual: Manifest and artifact can be jointly replaced.

threats.name: Manifest tampering
threats.impact: Scope, checks, commit, or limitations may be falsified.
threats.current_detection: Structural validation; digest changes only if a separately retained digest is compared.

threats.name: False execution provenance
threats.impact: A commit or command may be claimed without the replay actually executing under it.
threats.residual: Manifest is not an execution attestation.

threats.name: Evidence omission
threats.impact: A relevant input, artifact, failed check, or limitation may be excluded.
threats.current_detection: Limited to reviewer comparison against protocol.
threats.residual: No completeness proof or automatically enumerated run inventory.

threats.name: Environment drift
threats.impact: Numerical behavior may differ across machines or dependency versions.
threats.current_detection: Basic platform and declared dependency metadata.
threats.residual: Not a lockfile or complete environment capture.

threats.name: Path ambiguity and symlink substitution
threats.impact: Hashing or review may refer to different files than intended.
threats.current_detection: File existence and digest check only.
threats.residual: Path canonicalization and symlink policy are not implemented.

security_objectives: Detect accidental or post-recording content changes when original files are retained
Make the manifest's limits explicit and prevent it from being mistaken for proof
Allow an independent reviewer to recompute content hashes
Avoid claiming authenticity, trusted time, completeness, or execution attestation without controls
next_controls_to_evaluate: Schema validation using a pinned JSON Schema engine in CI
Environment lockfile hash and complete dependency capture
Signed manifest with key ownership and verification procedure
Trusted timestamp or externally anchored signature
Immutable artifact retention and independent custody
CI attestation tying workflow run, source revision, and artifacts
